claims.text: The proposed baseline is an equimolar five-element refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline alloy forms a single-phase solid solution.
The baseline alloy has a superconducting critical temperature of approximately 5–8 K.
At least 5 at% Sc will be introduced by arc melting and rapid solidification.
Sc addition modifies local bonding in the refractory HEA.
Sc addition increases the electronic density of states near the Fermi level.
The increased density of states raises Tc relative to the undoped baseline.
Local compositional variation and short-range order affect superconducting behavior through structural disorder.
Local compositional variation and short-range order alter electron-phonon coupling.
Local compositional variation and short-range order alter the density of states near the Fermi level.
Sc addition reduces partial chemical ordering.
Sc addition increases the effective valence electron concentration.
Valence electron concentration is associated with Tc in high-entropy-alloy superconductors.
Increasing effective valence electron concentration strengthens BCS-type electron-phonon interactions and thereby increases Tc.
Sc-doped samples will have a Tc approximately 0.5–1 K above the undoped baseline.
Sc-doped samples will have a larger superconducting volume fraction than the undoped baseline.
Secondary-phase formation or phase segregation may suppress the Tc enhancement or make it non-monotonic.
The predicted effect is restricted to compositions that remain single-phase solid solutions.
The magnitude of the Tc increase depends on local chemical order and phase stability.
No Tc increase, or a Tc decrease, in a single-phase Sc-containing sample would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention describe Sc as an additional element, which would turn the five-element baseline into a six-element alloy, whereas the experiment describes 5 and 10 at% Sc substitution, implying replacement of one or more baseline elements. The compositional operation is therefore inconsistent or underspecified.
